svg.aria-label: D07 Intelligence ownership and signal lifecycle
svg.title: D07 Intelligence ownership and signal lifecycle
svg.text: Owns features, baselines, exceedances, diagnostic candidates, RUL
✕ Must not decide fleet priority or notify users.
Owns every actionable signal, telemetry freshness and fleet-attention
✕ Must not recompute HUMS maths; reads HUMS rows.
Owns nothing persistent: bulk distributions over M7 and HUMS rows.
✕ Must not score health or create signals.
Owns the fleet control-center view: per-asset decision summary.
✕ Must not become a second signal source or vocabulary.
Owns conversation context; reads through authorised tools.
✕ Must not create, close or reword signals as fact.
Every transition is a human action through the lifecycle API and writes an audit event (_audit_transition). Signals are created only by M7
sync (today triggered by reads — F6), never by LISA.
How duplicates and conflicts are prevented
1 · One owner per signal type (M7) — other modules read.
2 · Deterministic signal_key per source fact; concurrent sync inserts under SAVEPOINT and adopts
3 · HUMS evaluation serialised per sensor (advisory lock): one exceedance, one finding.
4 · M14-ext reads persisted rows; never calls write-on-read HUMS functions.
5 · Proposed: signal-type registry, status filters from model constants, sync moved to jobs (F6, F7).
D07 · INTELLIGENCE OWNERSHIP — HUMS · M7 · M14-ext · M4.2 · LISA
condition still true on next sync → stays / re-opens
